caption: One cancelled wedding and my whole month shifted. How do you budget when your income isn't the same twice?

slides.title:
How I spend my
R21 300 p/m
freelance income
Living in Plettenberg Bay
slides.body:
Female, 29
Single, shares a two bedroom with a flatmate
Job: Freelance wedding videographer
Net income: R21 300 p/m (this month, one wedding cancelled)

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Half of a two bedroom flat, water
slides.body: Cheaper than a one bedroom, and it means I can't ignore someone else's rent.

slides.title: Equipment payments
slides.includes: Camera body and drone on a store payment plan
slides.body: I'm paying for the drone that I used on two shoots.

slides.title: Petrol
slides.includes: Driving to venues across the Garden Route
slides.body: A wedding in Knysna and one in George in the same weekend is R900 of petrol.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Spar, and what's left of a client's catering
slides.body: Leftover wedding food is a real line in my budget.

slides.title: Tax set-aside
slides.includes: A separate account for SARS provisional tax
slides.body: Moved over the day after a client pays. If I leave it, it gets spent.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Editing software, electricity, phone, funeral policy, stokvel, black tax, eating out
slides.body: Eating out is R1 600 this month. I celebrated a booking that then cancelled.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R21 300. Last month was R34 000. The rent doesn't know which month it is.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it showed my income and spending side by side for the month.

The eating out line was after the cancellation.

No bank login needed.
